topics.title: Remote access and self-hosting infrastructure
topics.summary: Rust-native remote desktop, VCS, and terminal tools enabling decentralized device access, version control, and CLI workflows without reliance on centralized services. Emphasis on performance, privacy, and user control.

topics.title: AI knowledge management and workflow automation
topics.summary: Self-hosted LLM-backed platforms for document indexing, prompt management, and multi-step workflow orchestration. Combines semantic search, agent reasoning, and automation without vendor lock-in.

topics.title: Performance-native developer tools in Rust
topics.summary: High-velocity linters, formatters, and CLI utilities written in Rust that replace established Python/Node.js tools by orders of magnitude in speed and resource efficiency.

topics.title: Developer-native observability and status monitoring
topics.summary: Tools for tracking system health, API uptime, and development workflow changes in real-time. Combines monitoring, alerting, and change detection for operational insight and debugging.

topics.title: Collaborative project management and knowledge workspaces
topics.summary: Self-hosted platforms for team coordination, document management, knowledge capture, and privacy-first collaboration. Integrates AI agents alongside human workflow.

whats_new: Remote access and self-hosting has solidified as a foundational theme, with Rust-native tooling dominating (RustDesk, jj-vcs, Tabby). AI knowledge management has emerged as distinct from generic orchestration—platforms now combine semantic search, agent reasoning, and prompt management as integrated systems. Developer observability (status pages, change detection, security) clusters as a new theme reflecting maturation of DevOps practices. Collaborative knowledge workspaces have ascended, displacing last week's generic backend-as-a-platform focus with privacy-first, AI-augmented alternatives.

projects.title: Rust VCS Integration Bridge with Conflict Resolution UI
projects.pitch: Build a CLI that wraps jj-vcs with a TUI for viewing and resolving merge conflicts visually, supporting undo/redo history replay and collaborative conflict resolution hints via inline diffs. Export conflict metadata as JSON for CI integration.
projects.why_now: jj-vcs is trending as a Git alternative; teams need UX tooling to make its advanced features accessible to non-experts.

projects.title: LLM-Powered Document Ingestion Pipeline with Semantic Tagging
projects.pitch: Write a Python async daemon that monitors a local directory, auto-extracts text from PDFs/images via OCR, generates embeddings and semantic tags via local LLMs (Ollama), and indexes into a SQLite FOSS vector store. Expose a simple HTTP API for retrieval.
projects.why_now: AI knowledge management platforms are trending; organizations need lightweight, self-contained ingestion without external APIs.

projects.title: Multi-Metric Health Dashboard Aggregator for Micro-Services
projects.pitch: Create a Go CLI that scrapes health endpoints from multiple services (Gatus, custom endpoints), aggregates metrics into a unified dashboard, and emits alerts via webhooks when thresholds are breached. Include a minimal web UI showing service topology and incident timeline.
projects.why_now: Developer observability tools are trending; teams need to correlate signals across fragmented monitoring systems.

projects.title: Rust CLI Latency Regression Detector with GitHub PR Annotations
projects.pitch: Build a Rust benchmarking harness that measures latency of CLI tools (ruff, jj, k9s) across commits, detects regressions via statistical testing, and posts annotations to GitHub PRs with before/after timings and blame info.
projects.why_now: Performance-native Rust tools are trending; maintainers need automated regression detection to preserve sub-millisecond guarantees.

projects.title: Prompt Version Control System with A/B Test Framework
projects.pitch: Develop a Git-like system for managing prompt versions, enabling teams to track prompt evolution, compare outputs across versions via LLM evaluation metrics, and A/B test prompts in production with gradual rollout. Include CLI and Python SDK for CI integration.
projects.why_now: Prompt management platforms are trending; teams need versioning discipline for prompts the way they version code.

projects.title: End-to-End Encrypted Remote Device Sync with Bandwidth Awareness
projects.pitch: Build a Rust service that syncs files between RustDesk-connected devices using CRDT, encrypts in transit with TLS, and adapts transfer rates based on real-time bandwidth via congestion detection. Support selective sync rules and conflict resolution via last-write-wins or user intervention.
projects.why_now: Self-hosted remote access is trending; teams need efficient, encrypted data sync that respects network constraints.

projects.title: Unified Security Event Aggregator with Automated Response Chains
projects.pitch: Develop a Go service that ingests security events from CrowdSec, Gitleaks, and custom scanners, correlates them by asset/severity, and auto-triggers remediation chains (secret rotation, firewall rule updates, incident ticket creation) via pluggable handlers. Include audit logging and rollback support.
projects.why_now: Developer security observability is trending; teams need coordinated response to multi-signal attacks rather than siloed alerts.

projects.title: AI-Augmented Team Inbox for Knowledge Workspace
projects.pitch: Build a notification aggregator that surfaces relevant knowledge base documents, project updates, and AI-generated summaries in a unified inbox. Use semantic search to surface context-aware docs when teammates mention topics, and enable AI-powered suggested responses.
projects.why_now: Collaborative knowledge platforms are trending; teams need AI to surface relevant context without forcing manual search.

projects.title: Rust Performance Profiler with Comparative Benchmarking
projects.pitch: Develop a comprehensive profiling framework for Rust CLI tools that tracks CPU, memory, I/O, and latency at microsecond granularity across versions. Generate public HTML reports comparing performance across tools and regressions, integrate with GitHub for trend visualization, and support custom metric collection via plugins.
projects.why_now: Performance-native Rust tooling is trending; the ecosystem needs standardized profiling infrastructure to track progress and motivate optimization.

projects.title: Self-Hosted Multi-Tenant Knowledge Graph with Semantic Reasoning
projects.pitch: Build a full-featured knowledge management platform that ingests documents, automatically constructs entity graphs, enables semantic queries via SPARQL-like syntax, and uses LLMs to infer relationships and answer questions by reasoning over the graph. Include multi-tenant isolation, role-based access, and export to standard knowledge formats.
projects.why_now: AI knowledge management is trending; organizations need semantic reasoning over documents, not just keyword search.

projects.title: Privacy-First Team Collaboration Platform with AI Co-Pilot
projects.pitch: Develop a self-hosted workspace combining task management, document collaboration, real-time chat, and embedded AI co-pilots (agent-driven task suggestions, auto-summarization, code review assistance). Include end-to-end encryption, offline-first syncing via CRDT, and granular permission models.
projects.why_now: Collaborative platforms are trending with AI augmentation; teams need privacy-first alternatives that retain control of data and AI reasoning.

projects.title: Distributed Remote Device Registry with Zero-Trust Discovery
projects.pitch: Create a decentralized registry for RustDesk/Tailscale endpoints using Raft consensus and mDNS gossip, enabling devices to discover and authenticate peers without a central server. Include reputation scoring, automatic failover, and peer-to-peer tunneling with multi-hop relay support.
projects.why_now: Self-hosted remote access is trending; teams need resilient discovery that survives infrastructure failures and vendor outages.

projects.title: Observability Anomaly Detector with ML-Driven Alert Tuning
projects.pitch: Build a machine learning system that ingests metrics from Gatus and CrowdSec, learns baseline distributions, detects anomalies via isolation forests, and auto-tunes alert thresholds to minimize false positives while catching real issues. Include root cause inference and correlations across metric domains.
projects.why_now: Developer observability is trending; teams are overwhelmed by alert noise and need intelligent filtering that learns from patterns.
